_what: Which of the gateway's 110 MCP tools this workspace exposes. mcp-proxy.mjs filters tools/list against `allow` and refuses a tools/call to anything outside it. Adding a capability is a one-line edit here — the list is meant to grow.
_measured: 2026-09-08, over Streamable HTTP after the dashboard transport was switched from stdio. Every entry below was called and its answer read; nothing is here on the strength of its description.
_cost: 12 tools, 5,814 bytes of schema on every request of every session. Down from 17 tools / 8,122 bytes earlier the same day, from 36 / 17,563 before that, and from 110 / 55,295 unfiltered. Re-measure with `node probes/measure-allowlist.mjs` after any edit here — that script filters the live tools/list exactly as the proxy does and prints the per-tool bytes, so a removal can be judged against what it buys. The saving is per request, not per session, so it compounds with step count.

_read_these_with_care._when: 2026-09-08, third pass. These three stay in the list because their detail is genuinely useful, but each reports at least one field that is simply wrong, and a wrong number acted on is worse than a missing one.
_read_these_with_care.omniroute_check_quota: Still wrong after autoRefreshProviderQuota was switched on 2026-09-08 — re-called immediately afterwards and it reports the same figures, so the setting does not fix it. Reports percentRemaining 100 and tokenStatus 'valid' for all six connections — including Cline, which is out of credit, and Kilo Code, which returns empty answers. It reads the connection record, not the seat's real standing. Never route off it. There is no working quota endpoint behind it: /dashboard/quota shows 'No Providers Connected' because quota tracking is OAuth-only and every live seat is API-key.
_read_these_with_care.omniroute_cost_report: Its byProvider and byModel tables are real and are the only place the per-seat success rates appear. Its top-level totalCost, requestCount and tokenCount are all 0 regardless, so the summary contradicts the detail directly underneath it. ⚠️ The reply is roughly 9,000 tokens with no way to narrow it — call it when the per-seat numbers are the point, not to check a total.
_read_these_with_care.omniroute_get_session_snapshot: topModels is real. requestCount, costTotal and tokenCount stayed 0 immediately after two successful chat completions, and every entry in topProviders is labelled 'unknown'. Treat everything but the model histogram as unpopulated.

_pruned_and_why._when: 2026-09-08, second pass. Each tool below was called first; the reason is what its own answer said, not a guess. Restoring any one of them is a one-line edit.
_pruned_and_why.local_corpus_status/search/read (1,733 b: Reports configured:false with source:null, and there is no dashboard setting or /api/settings key that would configure it — the Context Sources tab holds only Notion and Obsidian. Its own limits settle it regardless: maxTotalBytes 67,108,864 and maxFileBytes 1,048,576. The the source corpus corpus is 2.7 GB of 79-332 MB PDFs, so the index could not hold one book even if a root existed. The earlier note that its root was 'one dashboard setting away' was wrong.
_pruned_and_why.omniroute_ccr_store/retrieve/inspect/lis: Answers storage:memory with 0 entries. Nothing in this workspace writes to it and the store does not survive a gateway restart, so six tools were carrying a cache that is always empty.
_pruned_and_why.omniroute_rtk_discover/learn (1,158 byte: sampleCount 0, candidates empty. RTK already runs locally as a Bash hook (Tools/rtk/rtk.exe); these sample gateway traffic that this workspace does not generate.
_pruned_and_why.omniroute_pool_status/pool_health (911 b: totalPools 0, providers empty. Pools belong to the browser-session area, which is barred.
_pruned_and_why.omniroute_browser_pool_status (476 bytes: browserRunning false, stealthAvailable false. The Playwright binary behind it must not be installed, so the status can never become interesting.
_pruned_and_why.omniroute_compression_status/compression: enabled:false, strategy:'off'. Compression stays off by decision, so these report a constant.
_pruned_and_why.omniroute_memory_search (525 bytes): 0 memories. omniroute_memory_add is blocked as mutating, so nothing will ever write to the store this reads.
_pruned_and_why.omniroute_skills_list (340 bytes): Empty registry. The standing rule is to read a manual when the job arrives and install nothing, which keeps it empty.
_pruned_and_why._third_pass: 2026-09-08, after /api/combos was read directly for the first time. It returns {combos: [], total: 0} and /api/combos/metrics returns {}, so the hand-made combo list is empty — and five allowlisted tools were sitting on top of that empty table. Each was called to confirm rather than inferred from the endpoint.
_pruned_and_why._fourth_pass_correction: 2026-09-08, later the same day. The third pass drew the wrong conclusion from a right measurement. /api/combos is empty, but /api/combos/AUTO returns 40+ BUILT-IN combos — auto, auto/coding, auto/vision, auto/coding:reliable and the rest — each with a candidate pool of up to 8 seats, comboStrategy 'fallback' and routerStrategy 'lkgp'. The combo subsystem is not unconfigured; it ships configured. These five tools stay pruned anyway, and now for a better reason: every one of them reads the hand-made list only and cannot see the built-in combos. Verified by calling each directly over HTTP with probes/mcpcall.mjs, bypassing this allow list: omniroute_list_combos returns {combos: []}, and omniroute_best_combo_for_task with a valid taskType ('coding' — the enum is coding|review|planning|analysis|debugging|documentation, not the free-text 'task' the earlier test passed) still answers 'No enabled combos available'. The combos are reached by naming them as a MODEL ID in a chat completion, which needs no MCP tool and costs no schema bytes. That is why the allow list did not grow.
_pruned_and_why.omniroute_best_combo_for_task (619 bytes: Errors: 'No enabled combos available'. The largest of the five, and the one that looked most useful.
_pruned_and_why.omniroute_get_combo_metrics (351 bytes): Needs a comboId, and no combo exists to name.
_pruned_and_why.omniroute_simulate_route (554 bytes): Errors: 'No matching combo found' for a live model id with a token estimate.
_pruned_and_why.omniroute_explain_route (392 bytes): Tested properly rather than assumed: a real chat completion was made through the gateway and its X-Request-Id fed straight back in. It answered with every field 'unknown' and the note 'Routing decision not found. The /api/routing/decisions endpoint may not be implemented yet'. So it fails on a genuine, seconds-old request id — it is not waiting for traffic, the store behind it does not exist.
_pruned_and_why._the_five_together: 2,308 bytes per request, 28% of what the list weighed. Restoring them means configuring combos first, and the note under _blocked_and_why/mutating still applies: that is the owner's, in the dashboard. See the README on why configuring them was judged not worth doing.

_blocked_and_why.unconfigured: obsidian_* (21) and notion_* (6) both answer "token not configured. Set it in Settings > Context Sources."
_blocked_and_why.policy: omniroute_x_search needs the xAI browser session, and browser-session seats are barred — an account ban is the owner's one redline. Same for omniroute_pool_warm and the browser pool launch calls.
_blocked_and_why.mutating: omniroute_create_combo, omniroute_switch_combo, omniroute_set_*, omniroute_sync_pricing, omniroute_cache_flush, omniroute_compression_configure, plugin_install/uninstall/activate/deactivate, omniroute_skills_enable/execute, omniroute_memory_add, obsidian writes. Gateway configuration is the owner's, not a session's.
_blocked_and_why.broken: omniroute_db_health_check still returns the SQLite driver error even over HTTP. omniroute_radar_catalog and omniroute_pick_fastest_model return upstream 404s — radar because RADAR_ENABLED is off and radarAdminUrl is null.
_blocked_and_why.noise: gamification_* (XP, badges, leaderboards) works but has nothing to do with any job here. omniroute_oneproxy_* fetches free proxy servers from a marketplace, not web pages — it is not a substitute for omniroute_web_fetch. omniroute_github_skills_search, _scan and _install are pruned for COST, not for uselessness — see _github_skills_ruling below. omniroute_web_fetch itself needs a Firecrawl/Jina/Tavily key; omniroute_web_search is free, verified against a live query on 2026-09-08, and allowed.
_blocked_and_why._github_skills_ruling: Owner ruling 2026-09-08: treat GitHub the way the OmniRoute skill manuals are treated — look at what is there, take only the part a live job needs, install nothing. The place it earns its keep is the research pass at the START of a workflow. An earlier note here said the search tool was merely rate-limited without a token; that was wrong. Measured 2026-09-08 with no token: it returns {"skills":[],"total":0} and the error 'GitHub API rate limited — add a GITHUB_TOKEN', so the token is the on-switch, not a speed-up. It is read from the gateway process environment, not from a /api/settings field — a scan of all 80+ settings keys for /github/ matched nothing — so it is a Windows user environment variable and the gateway must be restarted to see it. The three tools stay OUT of the allowlist all the same: measured at 921 + 672 + 881 = 2,474 bytes, adding them would be +43% on the 5,814-byte per-request payload, permanently, for a capability used at the start of a research pass. Call them on demand with probes/mcpcall.mjs instead — same pattern as every other pruned tool, and it costs nothing between uses. When they are used: search, then ALWAYS run _scan on anything before reading it further (it checks for hardcoded secrets, eval(base64) and os.system-style calls), and never call _install. TOKEN LIVE 2026-09-08 and verified — a query returned a real scored repo with no error. Two things measured at the same time, both worth knowing before relying on it. First, the token must reach the gateway through the PROCESS environment: the app's own ~/.omniroute/.env holds only STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY, and restarting the gateway from a terminal opened BEFORE the variable was created is not enough — the launching shell has to be new too. Second, the rate limit still bites hard even authenticated: roughly half a dozen queries in quick succession brought back the same 'add a GITHUB_TOKEN' error, because each query costs several upstream calls. It recovers on its own after a minute. So this is a few deliberate queries at the start of a research pass, never a sweep, and the error text is misleading — it means 'slow down', not 'no token'. Result quality on the first hit was poor (hasSkillFile false, a scraped description), so treat the output as a lead to check, not an index to trust.
_blocked_and_why._note: The whole db_backed group — list_models_catalog, memory_*, skills_*, plugin_*, compression_*, gamification_* — was blocked here until 2026-09-08 because the standalone stdio server could not open storage.sqlite. Switching the dashboard transport to Streamable HTTP fixed all thirteen: they now execute inside the live gateway, where the database is already open. The stdio spawn is still broken; the proxy no longer uses it.
